== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' appears in the original 1766 religious census return for Derryloran, County Tyrone. In the Drumearn section he is enumerated as ''John Glasco'', immediately after two separate entries for ''Jams Glasco''.<ref>National Archives of Ireland, Parliamentary Return 665, 1766 religious census for Derryloran, ''IHP/1/665'', [https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-IHP-1-665 original return and transcription], accessed 17 July 2026; independently transcribed in PRONI ''T808/15264''.</ref>

The return concerns householders by religion. It confirms John's residence at Drumearn and places him in a local Glasgow cluster, but gives no age or family relationship. The order of the entries does not establish that either James was his father or brother.

John Glasgow may be connected to [[Glasgow-1343|John Glasgow (abt.1738-)]], though further research is needed to confirm a relationship.

== Research Notes ==
* The 1740 Ulster religious return lists two William and two James Glasgow households at Derryloran, but does not name a child John or state any relationships.<ref>[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740religiousreturnsulstername.pdf 1740 Religious Returns, Ulster surname transcription], p. 119.</ref> Shared parish and suitable chronology do not identify either William as John's father.
* The two 1766 James entries and John's adjacent entry support a same-townland cluster only. Their relationships remain unproved.

A possible identification concerns John Glasco, charged at Bow Street. John Glasco, Esq., said he was an officer on the Staff and was brought before the Bow Street magistrate charged with wounding patrolman John Smith. The reported incident occurred on Tuesday night after the play in Covent Garden; Glasco was committed.<ref>The Times, 2 May 1799, p.3, Public Office, Bow Street; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/32820363/ record].</ref> Allegation and committal are not conviction. Military status is self-reported and unconfirmed; no Irish origin or kin is stated. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glascow, London chairman. John Glascow, a chairman, said he saw a man in black running with pistols after Martha Ray was shot in Covent Garden.<ref>Derby Mercury, provider-labelled 19 March 1779, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/394231375/ record]; Old Bailey original, printed p.207; [https://www.dhi.ac.uk/san/ob/1770s/177904040005.gif record]; Old Bailey Proceedings, James Hackman record t17790404-3; event dating only; [https://www.oldbaileyonline.org/record/t17790404-3 record].</ref> The Old Bailey indictment specifies that Martha Ray was shot on 7 April 1779 (printed p.207); that is the event date, not the indictment or newspaper publication date. The newspaper describes evidence after the shooting, not established trial testimony. Its March provider label is incorrect. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Loughinsholin freeholder, 1831. The 16 August 1831 declaration lists Robert Glasgow and John Glasgow among freeholders of the barony printed Loughinshollen (modern Loughinsholin), County Londonderry, supporting Sir Robert Bateson. They are co-signatories; no kinship, occupation, age or individual townland is given. Castledawson and 4 July 1831 refer to the opposing meeting discussed in the declaration, not their homes or their signing date.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 16 August 1831, p.3, Loughinshollen freeholders’ declaration; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390548642/ record].</ref> [[Glasgow-2058]], [[Glasgow-3927]] (an indexed freeholder with uncertain locality), [[Glasgow-2990]] and [[Glasgow-4090]] remain adult regional comparisons. No same-name co-signature establishes descent, brotherhood or identity with the Cookstown merchant. The declaration concerns a holding in the barony, not necessarily residence there. The identification remains uncertain.
